newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt plans work-for-dole scheme.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt plans work-for-dole scheme.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Sunday his government may introduce a work-for-dole scheme in an attempt to reduce youth unemployment.
"This approach is not designed to save money, and it's not designed to manipulate the unemployment figures," Howard said a television interview on Channel Nine's Sunday programme.
He said young people could take part in up to 30 compulsory and voluntary pilot schemes mainly in rural and regional areas where youth unemployment is at its highest.

Details of the schemes have yet to be finalised, but Howard said young people who took part in the projects would be paid at award rates and work between 15 or 20 hours a week to earn the equivalent of their unemployment benefits.
The Prime Minister said young people would not be exploited, and denied the projects had any similarity to the A$3-an-hour youth wage policy taken by the coalition to the 1993 election.
"What it will do is provide people with work, generated by local business and community groups in areas of high unemploymment ... there will be no question of people being exploited," Howard said.
He did not say what specific work-for-dole schemes his government had planned, but added one scheme may include young people working for volunteer community organisations by helping retired people.
"This is one way of tackling the problem and I don't see it in any way annihilating the 30,000 long term or the 100,000 overall youth unemployment in the community," he said.
The Australian Bureau of Statistics is to release January's employment data on Thursday, with most economists forecasting no change from December's unemployment rate of 8.6 percent.
